concept_options.title: The Pantry Door
concept_options.hook: A little door, a little thief, and a papa who always knows.
concept_options.visual_approach: Two-character flat cartoon in a warm kitchen. The pantry door is the recurring stage: Johny tiptoes in and out of frame through it, Papa leans in to peek. Simple silhouettes, rounded shapes, honey-and-cream palette with coral accents. Every line of the rhyme gets a physical beat: tiptoe, eat, wipe nose, peek, giggle, run.
concept_options.target_audience: Toddlers and preschoolers (1-5) plus parents who grew up with the rhyme
key_points: Full traditional rhyme, all 12 lines, in order
Two distinct voices: child (Johny) and warm adult (Papa)
Every dialogue line paired with a readable character action
Big friendly captions so pre-readers can follow along
concept_options.core_message: A cozy, giggly bedtime-style take on the classic rhyme
grounded_in: character-animation pipeline supports 2-character local rigged acting
Piper local TTS provides two distinct English voices at $0
concept_options.why_this_works: The rhyme is inherently a two-character call-and-response, which is exactly the MVP sweet spot (1-2 characters) the character-design director skill recommends. The pantry door gives one strong recurring framing device, keeping the scene system coherent per the scene director's complexity budget.

concept_options.title: Karaoke Kitchen
concept_options.hook: The whole rhyme bounces to the beat, one big word at a time.
concept_options.visual_approach: Music-driven version: a simple ukulele-style backing track carries the rhythm, characters bounce and gesture to the beat, and karaoke-style word-by-word captions dominate the lower third. Characters are smaller, captions are the hero.
key_points: Word-level karaoke captions as the visual hero
concept_options.core_message: A bouncy, sing-along version of the rhyme
grounded_in: karaoke caption burn is a Remotion-only feature per the HyperFrames decision matrix
local music synthesis is simpler for a steady beat than for a lullaby
concept_options.why_this_works: Strong for short-form retention, but word-level karaoke captions are explicitly Remotion-only in this project's decision matrix, and the music-driven beat is harder to fake with synthesized audio. More moving parts for the same story.

concept_options.title: Bedtime Johny
concept_options.hook: Night falls, the kitchen glows, and the little thief gets caught.
concept_options.visual_approach: A moonlit night kitchen: deep blues and warm lamp-glow, a moon visible through the window, stars. The same beats as c1 but with a calm, lullaby mood and slower pacing. More atmospheric, less bouncy.
key_points: Night palette with warm lamp glow
Same two-character cast and beats as c1
grounded_in: same rig as c1, only palette and pacing change
synthesized lullaby music fits a slow tempo better
concept_options.why_this_works: Differentiates on mood, but a darker night palette is harder to keep readable for pre-readers and for caption contrast. c1's bright daytime kitchen is the safer, more legible choice for the target age.

selected_concept.rationale: Agent recommendation pending user approval: c1 is the strongest fit for the pipeline's 2-character sweet spot, keeps one coherent scene system (the pantry door), and the bright palette maximizes caption legibility for pre-readers. c2 is a good fallback if the user wants a punchier short-form cut; c3 is a mood variant of c1 that can be revisited later with the same rigs.

stages.approach: Public-domain nursery rhyme; technique references: flat 2D character shorts (Cocomelon-style silhouette simplicity) and the project's own Ink Theater as a local-motion reference. Feasibility confirmed: 2 characters, simple rig, no physical contact beats.

stages.approach: Write the 12-line rhyme as action beats with per-line emotion/gaze/pose notes. Generate 2 sample lines per character for voice approval.
stages.fallback_if_unavailable: if a Piper voice is unintelligible, swap to the other downloaded voice or adjust length_scale

stages.approach: Define Johny and Papa: silhouettes, palette, emotions (happy, mischievous, surprised, giggly, warm, amused), actions (tiptoe, eat, wipe, peek, giggle, run, lean, ruffle).
stages.fallback_if_unavailable: hand-author the spec JSON to the same schema

stages.approach: SVG rig parts (body, head, eyes, brows, mouth, arms, legs, hair, apron for Papa) with pivots, layer order, constraints, and named poses for every required action.
stages.fallback_if_unavailable: hand-author rig JSON to the same schema

stages.approach: Map the 12 lines to ~8 scenes: establish kitchen, sneak-in, eat, call-and-response x4, peek, reveal, giggle, run-off + end card. One establishing shot, action beats, reaction beats, resolution - per the complexity budget.

local lullaby music bed synthesis (Pixabay blocked 403, no AI music keys)

quality_tradeoffs.tradeoff: Piper local TTS (free, robotic-ish) vs cloud TTS like ElevenLabs (expressive, ~$0.10-0.30)
quality_tradeoffs.recommendation: Use Piper. No cloud API keys exist in this sandbox, and Piper's two voices are clearly distinct (child-ish vs warm adult).
quality_tradeoffs.quality_impact: Voices sound synthetic rather than expressive; acceptable for a nursery-rhyme test production.

quality_tradeoffs.tradeoff: Local FFmpeg-synthesized lullaby (free, simple) vs AI music (Suno/ElevenLabs, unavailable)
quality_tradeoffs.recommendation: Synthesize a gentle ukulele-style chord arpeggio with soft dynamics.
quality_tradeoffs.quality_impact: Music is simple and loopable rather than composed; it sits low under dialogue so the impact is small.

quality_tradeoffs.tradeoff: SVG flat characters (local, crisp, fully controllable) vs AI-generated character images (unavailable - no image gen keys)
quality_tradeoffs.recommendation: Hand-authored SVG rigs in the flat-motion-graphics style.
quality_tradeoffs.quality_impact: Characters are simple cartoon shapes, not richly illustrated; this is the pipeline's native path and stays crisp at 1080p.

alternative_paths.description: Free local path (this proposal): Piper TTS + SVG rigs + HyperFrames + FFmpeg music
Premium path (if API keys are added later): ElevenLabs voices + Suno music + FLUX character art
alternative_paths.what_changes: expressive voices, composed music, illustrated characters; same pipeline and runtime

production_plan.art_direction: Warm flat cartoon: cream/honey/coral palette, thick rounded outlines, simple two-tone characters, cozy kitchen with pantry door as the stage. Motion language: bouncy anticipation-overshoot springs, squash-and-stretch on bounces, holds on every dialogue line. Signature device: the pantry door as a framing proscenium. Big rounded sans captions in cream with coral highlight.

music_source.mood_direction: gentle lullaby, ukulele-style arpeggio, warm and slow

voice_selection.rationale: Only TTS available in this sandbox (no cloud keys). Two acoustically distinct voices: lessac = brighter/younger, alan = warmer/lower. Both tested and intelligible.
voice_selection.delivery_style: Johny: bright, quick, slightly mischievous. Papa: warm, slow, gentle, amused.
voice_selection.pacing_policy: Papa lines slightly slower (length_scale 1.05) with clear call-out phrasing; Johny lines quicker (0.95) with a giggle-friendly cadence. 0.3s sentence silence.

line_items.notes: local synth; Pixabay 403-blocked from this sandbox

approval.user_notes: Awaiting user approval of concept c1, runtime (hyperframes), free local tool path, and the 10-15s sample-first plan.

metadata.sample_plan: Before full production: render a 10-15s sample containing Johny (one expression change + tiptoe action), Papa (lean-in + call-out), the kitchen background, one dialogue line per character, and the music bed. User approves sample before batch asset generation.
metadata.honest_limitations: 1) Voices are synthetic (Piper), not expressive cloud TTS. 2) Music is a simple synthesized lullaby, not a composed track. 3) Characters are flat SVG cartoons, not illustrated. 4) character-animation pipeline is marked beta in this project. 5) No AI image/video generation is available in this sandbox (no API keys), so all visuals are locally authored SVG - which is the pipeline's native path anyway.
